newsitem.title: singapore: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were little changed on Wednesday in lacklustre trade with most traders sidelined ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins congressional testimony today, dealers said.
Greenspan will deliver the first leg of his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins address today. The second part will take place on March 5.
"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning on some position adjustments. All eyes are on the outcome of Alan Greespan's speech tonight," a local dealer said.
"Everyone is waiting for Greenspan to give some clues to which way the market is headed," he said.

In day-to-day rates, Wednesday/Thursday was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent but Thursday/Friday and week-fixed eased 1/16 percentage point each to a common 5-5/16 5-3/16 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent and three-months unchanged at 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent, nine-months was unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 and twelve-months unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent.
